reason: Attacked and it held. I downloaded the OCR of archive.org item cu31924016872172 and read its title page: LOCKE'S ESSAY CONCERNING HUMAN UNDERSTANDING, collated and annotated by Alexander Campbell Fraser, Clarendon Press, M.DCCC.XCIV, VOL. II. So the named edition is the one that was opened. At the head of CHAPTER XIX, [OF ENTHUSIASM], the text reads: He that would seriously set upon the search of truth, ought in the first place to prepare his mind with a love of it. The comma after truth is there, so the verifier's correction is right and not an invention: the wording ships as the named edition prints it. The marginal note beside it reads Love of Truth necessary, exactly as the locator claims. The page is right too, and I checked it three ways: the table of contents of the second volume gives XIX. [Of Enthusiasm] . . . 428; the running head on the preceding page is Faith and Reason. 427 and on the following page Enthusiasm. 429; and the index entry reads love of truth, 428. Section 1 is right: Fraser opens the chapter with the bracketed section number 1. Fraser's footnote to that sentence begins This chapter was added in the fourth edition and quotes Locke to Molyneux of April 1695, so the note's claim that Of Enthusiasm is not in the Essay of 1690 is supported by the edition itself; the fourth edition is 1700. Attribution: Locke's own prose, not a character, no misattribution trap in the brief touches it. shipped.js returns no exact match, no near match, john locke at 0 for the year, not banned. Scope: philosophy, first published 1700, no scripture, no oratory, no content warning. Form checks: the source line is 131 characters, leads with the author's name, has no em dash; the quotation ends in a full stop and contains no straight double quote; the note has no em dash; the tag Philosophy is the form of the work.
